'''Douglas County Correctional Center''' ('''DCCC''') is a jail in [[Omaha, Nebraska]].  The jail is the largest in the Midwest and is operated by the [[Douglas County, Nebraska|Douglas County]] Department of Corrections.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url = http://www.dccorr.com/corrections/|title = Department of Corrections of Douglas County|date = |accessdate = November 5, 2014|website = dccorr.com |publisher = Douglas County and the City of Omaha|last = |first = }}</ref>  The jail is used to house inmates in criminal or immigration related offenses. The jail is located at 710 S. 17th St, Omaha, Nebraska.

== Timeline ==

Douglas County Correctional Center was opened in July 1979. It was designed with 12 housing units that held a total of 200 single bed cells.<ref name=":0" />

By 1983, the majority of the single cells were double bunked to bring the capacity to 363 beds.<ref name=":0" />

In April 1989, the annex was added to the Correctional Center. Eight dormitory style housing units were added with 354 beds and 2 isolation cells. This brought the capacity to 719 beds.<ref name=":0" />

In June 2005, construction of the Correctional Center was completed, adding nine housing units with 62 beds each and a medical housing unit that can accommodate a combination of 61 male and female inmates. This brings total capacity to 1,453 beds.<ref name=":0" />
